ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Canadian Consolidated List (Global Affairs Canada), United Nations Security Council sanctions, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Special Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU consolidated sanctions, and domestic Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) lists. FINTRAC requires enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs, heads of state, senior officials, and family members. The screening protocol must be completed before incorporation, with audit trail and risk rating documented; negative screening confirms no match to sanctions, terrorism, or PEP-related risk.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Mandatory for provincial Quebec incorporation; for federal CBCA incorporation: Corporations Canada 'beta' online portal with NUANS Name Search and Pre-Clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Quebec law mandates French as the primary language for corporate names under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11). The legal name must be in French; English-only names are prohibited unless accompanied by a French version. A non-French name can be used if it is a recognized trademark or the corporate name is composed of elements clearly descriptive in French. All corporate documents, name reservation requests, and registry filings must be transliterated into French script and the 'forme juridique' suffix (Inc., Corp., Ltée, etc.) must appear in an acceptable form. The name must be distinctive, not confusing with existing registered names, and not falsely imply government, professional, or regulated status.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Corporation under federal or provincial 'Act of Parliament' words requiring prior ministerial or regulatory consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 30 days of the refusal, pursuant to the Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises. For federal name pre-clearance rejection, an appeal may be made to the Director General of Corporations Canada within 30 days, providing evidence of distinctiveness and proof that the proposed name was rejected erroneously. A legal submission, including trademark search report or descriptive rationale, must be attached. If administrative appeal fails, the applicant may seek judicial review at the Québec Court (civil route) or the Federal Court, depending on whether the incorporation is provincial or federal, within 30 days of the administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible as 'registered office only' for incorporation and statutory mail receipt, provided a physical service address is held by the registered agent in Quebec. However, for Amazon FBA operations without physical premises, the registered office must be a real street address in Quebec where process serving is possible; a PO Box is prohibited. Any use of a shared virtual office must include a registered agent agreement and clear signage rights, but for the low-risk e-commerce marketplace business, no operational physical presence is required. Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency may accept a registered office as permanent establishment only if actual business activity is carried on there; for Amazon FBA third-party logistics, P/E risk is generally limited to business decision-making location of the company's officers.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to medium (15-30% risk within the first two years) – unannounced on-site inspections by the Registraire d'entreprises du Québec or CRA are primarily triggered by inconsistent filings, nominee director indicators, unexplained changes in address, or high-risk payment rails. For a standard low-risk Amazon FBA seller with proper corporate records and no physical office, the probability of an unannounced inspection is 15% during year one, increasing to 25–30% if the declared registered office is a shared virtual office with suspect conditions. The Loi sur la publicité légale des entreprises authorizes verification visits, and failure to permit a lawful inspection may lead to cancellation of registration and administrative penalties.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — GST/HST and corporate income tax registration and filing via Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca; master identifier is the Business Number (BN) with program-account suffixes. Provincial (Quebec): Revenu Québec — QST and provincial corporate tax registration and filing via the CLICK portal (clic.revenuquebec.ca); master identifier is the NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec). Customs: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers export reporting; CRA administers GST/HST on imported and exported goods.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) or the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA) to obtain a certificate of incorporation; provincial incorporation concurrently issues the NEQ. 2. Register federally with the CRA using Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts) or electronically through BRO to obtain the BN, the GST/HST program account (RT suffix), and the corporate income tax account (RC suffix). 3. Register with Revenu Québec through the Registraire des entreprises or the CLICK portal for the QST account (TVQ number), the Quebec corporate income tax account, and Quebec employer source deductions; registration is effective as of the earlier of the date commercial activity begins in Quebec or the date of the first taxable supply in Quebec. 4. A non-resident corporation without a Canadian resident office must appoint an authorized representative for service of process (ETA s. 298; Civil Code of Quebec arts. 3144-3145); director, officer, and ultimate-ownership schedules must accompany all filings. 5. Keep all registrations current within 30 days of any corporate, address, activity, or ownership change, and file a final return and deregistration within 30 days of cessation of taxable activity. 6. For the Amazon FBA model, the Canadian corporation acting as seller of record is the registered supplier for GST/HST and QST; the federal platform deemed-supplier rules (ETA ss. 178.18-178.22) and Quebec mirror rules generally apply to non-resident platform sellers rather than to this resident CA_CORP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Canadian-resident Business Corporation is a separate taxpayer taxed under ITA Part I on worldwide income, with a federal general corporate rate of 15% (9% small-business rate on active business income up to CAD 500,000 if the corporation is a Canadian-controlled private corporation) and a Quebec general corporate rate of 11.5% (3.2% reduced rate for income eligible for the small-business deduction); combined headline rate approximates 26.5%. There is no look-through or transparent classification for federal or Quebec income-tax purposes. If the corporation were instead a non-resident corporation, it would be taxed only on Canadian-source business income (ITA s. 2(3)) and be exposed to an additional 25% Part XIV branch tax on its after-tax Canadian business income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists in Canada. Available statutory elections affecting entity or regime classification: (i) Non-Resident-Owned Investment Corporation (NRO) election under ITA s. 133, which substitutes Part I tax with a 25% Part XIV tax for passive investment holding (review when FBA treasury or IP-licensing functions are separated); (ii) functional-currency reporting election under ITA s. 261 (eligible corporations may report Canadian tax results in U.S. dollars); (iii) GST/HST Quick Method election (ETA s. 218) and the closely related corporation election (ETA s. 156) permitting combined net-tax accounting; (iv) joint venture election (ETA s. 273 and Quebec parallel) designating a single JV operator as the sole GST/QST registrant; (v) small-business deduction business-limit allocation agreement among associated CCPCs (ITA s. 125(3)); and (vi) various rebate and simplified-accounting elections for non-resident registrants. Hybrid mismatch election mechanisms are not available; Canada applies OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.4, 18.5) and the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA s. 245).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5.0% plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.975% — combined effective rate of 14.975% on taxable retail supplies of goods situated in Quebec; GST and QST are mirror regimes administered respectively by the CRA and Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold: mandatory GST/HST registration is triggered when worldwide taxable supplies (including supplies of associated persons) exceed CAD 30,000 in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters or in any single calendar quarter (ETA ss. 148(1), 240); the identical CAD 30,000 QST threshold applies under the QSTA. Non-residents carrying on commercial activity in Canada are also required to register. For Amazon FBA general retail, the threshold is quickly exceeded once Canadian consumer sales commence, so immediate registration and collection of GST plus QST is expected.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based invoice clearance exists in Canada. GST/HST invoices must disclose the supplier's name and BN or QST registration number, the date, a description of the supply, and the tax amount shown separately (ETA s. 223(1); parallel Quebec rule under the Tax Administration Act); simplified invoices are permitted for supplies under CAD 150. The Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Initiative (Peppol/BIS 3.0, operated under the Council of the Federation with CAN/XIS network access) is voluntary for B2B transactions and not yet mandated. Revenu Québec accepts standard EDI/XML and CLICK portal submissions without government pre-clearance of each invoice. Regardless of format, all underlying transaction, logistics, and payment records must be retained for CRA and Revenu Québec audit windows.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (a) goods — a registrant's supply of tangible personal property delivered in Canada to a carrier for export, or exported as soon as is reasonably possible after the consideration becomes due, provided the registrant keeps conclusive proof of export (ETA Schedule VI, Part V, ss. 1-2; parallel QST provisions); (b) services — a supply made to a non-resident person where the service is not in connection with real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada and the service is not performed for an individual present in Canada (ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7); and (c) digital retail services delivered remotely to non-residents. For an Amazon FBA operation, inventory physically located in Quebec and sold to Canadian end consumers is taxable at the combined 14.975% rate; only sales delivered to foreign destinations, supported by international transport documentation, or services rendered to offshore buyers qualify for zero-rating. Zero-rating is denied if the goods return to Canada, are consumed in Canada, or if the exporter cannot prove the goods left Canada within a reasonable period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Export Declaration (B13A) filed electronically through the Canada Export Reporting System (CERS) for shipments valued above CAD 2,000; courier low-value shipments may be evidenced by carrier manifest data

Signed commercial invoice or Amazon payment settlement report identifying the Canadian seller, the CA GST/HST and QST registration numbers, the Quebec ship-from fulfillment center, and the foreign consignee address
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or courier consignment note showing the Canadian shipper, foreign consignee, and terminal-exit scan; CBSA eManifest acknowledgment where applicable
Outbound customs broker certificate or CBSA export acceptance report confirming actual export
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT/MT103 credit advice, or bank statement evidencing foreign-currency settlement of the exported sale
Amazon FBA inventory movement report and carrier pickup scan records demonstrating physical removal of the goods from the Quebec fulfillment center
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess export zero-rating claims within the normal four-year reassessment window (ETA s. 298; Quebec Tax Administration Act s. 1018), extended to ten years where misrepresentation involves neglect or carelessness, and with no time limit for fraud. If conclusive proof of export is not substantiated, the full combined 14.975% GST plus QST is assessed on the invoice amount, input tax credits and any refunds are clawed back, and statutory interest at prescribed CRA/Revenu Québec quarterly rates accrues from the original filing date. Civil penalties include a 6% late-remittance penalty plus 1% per full month on the unremitted amount, false-statement penalties of 5% of the amount with an additional 5% for repeated defaults within five years, and a 50% gross-negligence penalty on the understated tax (ETA ss. 280(1), 281.1(1)-(2); ITA s. 163(2); Quebec TAA s. 1059). Criminal prosecution for export-invoice fraud or evasion can result in fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment (ETA s. 327; ITA s. 239; Quebec TAA s. 1056). The 180-day repatriation benchmark is not a codified statutory deadline in Canada but is treated as best practice for documentary substantiation and currency-control risk; all export proceeds should be settled and recorded in the corporate accounts at the applicable CRA exchange rate within that window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), Canada's central bank. Canada operates a clean floating exchange-rate regime under the Currency Act and the Exchange Fund Accounts framework; there is no standalone foreign-exchange-control administration agency. Prudential banking supervision is exercised by OSFI, AML/CFT and money-services-business registration by FINTRAC, cross-border currency declaration by CBSA, and payment clearing-lattice oversight by Payments Canada (Lynx and ACSS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Both current-account and capital-account items are fully convertible for the Canadian dollar; no prior approval, licensing, quota or repatriation restriction applies to profit remittance, dividend distribution or capital return by CA_CORP (Quebec business corporation). FBA marketplace proceeds received in USD/EUR/CNH may be converted at market rates and remitted freely, subject only to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (default 25%, treaty-reduced, e.g., 15% dividends to a US parent), deemed-dividend anti-avoidance rules, Investment Canada Act notification thresholds, and beneficial-ownership disclosure to the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None exist. Canada abolished exchange-control surrender and repatriation requirements in 1951; an ISIC 4791 marketplace exporter may retain 100% of proceeds in foreign currency and hold USD/EUR/CNH-operating accounts without mandatory conversion ratios or statutory timelines. Only transparency obligations apply: financial entities file FINTRAC EFT reports for wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, and travellers crossing the border with cash or bearer instruments of CAD 10,000 or more must declare to CBSA.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as an ancillary settlement rail (Payoneer, Wise, Airwallex, Stripe) for Amazon FBA USD payouts and China-route supplier disbursements; Low-Medium as the sole primary treasury account for an unlicensed offshore EMI. Canada issues no 'EMI' charter: non-resident e-money institutions must be FINTRAC-registered Money Services Businesses, and any provider of retail payment services in Canada must be registered as a payment service provider under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), administered by the Bank of Canada and effective November 2024. Offshore EMIs operating without FINTRAC registration and RPAA registration are treated as unlicensed deposit-taking arrangements and will not satisfy the OSFI-compliant banking profile expected for CA_CORP.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal statutory in-person mandate exists: FINTRAC PCMLTFA permits verification of director identity by remote audio-video or by two independent authorized identification media under corporate CDD. In Quebec Big-Six banking practice, however, most Schedule I banks require at least one director/signatory to attend an initial in-person interview at a branch or before a notary for newly incorporated e-commerce corporations whose ultimate beneficial owners are entirely non-resident. Fully remote account opening is attainable only through digital SME onboarding products (e.g., TD Small Business, BMO eBusiness, RBC digital) after the enterprise has delivered its NEQ, REQ attestation, and a clean AML profile; any credibility gap in the marketplace-cash-flow explanation triggers enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly registered Quebec corporation with non-resident beneficial ownership, no brick-and-mortar premises, and marketplace-only activity flagged as a possible shell or low-substance entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c. S-31.1); REQ attestation of registration (Attestation de mise a jour); 12-month UBO organizational chart with validated passports; executed Amazon FBA Business Solutions Agreement evidencing ISIC 4791 retail sales; Quebec GST/QST and federal income-tax account numbers; board minutes authorizing the banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Amazon 'Marketplace' receipts appear as aggregated anonymous payer transactions rather than named-customer invoices, raising trade-based money-laundering concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed seller agreement and Amazon settlement statements; FNSKU-level inventory ledger; purchase orders from FBA vendors; buyer-order logs extracted from Seller Central; shipment IDs and carrier bill-of-lading sets; customs entries filed by the licensed CBSA broker.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity micro-receipts in USD from payment aggregators (Payoneer, Stripe, Amazon Pay) without underlying commercial documents visible to the bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ERP sales ledger cross-referenced to payout statements; bank conversion confirmations; quarterly GST/QST and federal corporate returns; product-level gross-margin analysis demonstrating genuine e-commerce trade; funds-flow memorandum linking every inbound batch to an Amazon settlement ID.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large related-party or high-risk-jurisdiction disbursements to offshore FBA suppliers, particularly China-sourced inventory, triggering sanctions screening and trade-mismatch alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed supplier agreements; commercial-invoice/bill-of-lading/air-waybill document sets; OECD-compliant transfer-pricing documentation where suppliers are affiliated; FATCA/CRS self-certifications; sanctions-screening results showing no UN, OFAC, or OSFI-listed counterparties; enhanced due-diligence questionnaire completed by each material overseas vendor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident parent injects equity into CA_CORP via SWIFT MT103 (gpi with tracked UETR) with narrative purpose phrased as 'Injection of capital into wholly-owned Canadian operating subsidiary; equity subscription; not a purchase-price or service payment'. No central-bank authorization is required; the CAD/USD conversion is executed at the receiving Schedule I bank's prevailing market rate and credited same-day through Payments Canada Lynx. The bank's documentary package must include the directors' resolution authorizing share issuance, the executed subscription agreement, updated share register, REQ attestation, UBO and FATCA/CRS declarations, and, where the parent's contribution crosses prescribed thresholds, a post-closing Investment Canada Act notification; FINTRAC EFT reporting is triggered at CAD 10,000 or more.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlement for FBA inventory replenishment employs three clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 with mandatory UETR for ordinary commercial wires; (b) commercial documentary letters of credit (sight or term) for high-value purchase orders from overseas vendors; and (c) USD-denominated payments through US correspondent Nostro chains where the Canadian corporation maintains a USD clearing account. Domestic CAD treasury operations settle over Lynx (large-value real-time gross settlement) and the ACSS; retail refunds and marketplace disbursements ride ACH, EFT, and card rails (Amazon Pay, Stripe, Visa/Mastercard). Every outbound wire equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000 is captured by the bank's FINTRAC EFT-reporting framework, and the corporate treasury must retain underlying commercial documents for each disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (outright, forward-start and rolling forwards) in CAD/USD, CAD/EUR and CAD/CNH with a Canadian Schedule I bank under ISDA/CSA master agreements.

Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps with maturities aligned to FBA inventory replenishment cycles, governed by OSFI Guideline B-7 derivative risk-management requirements and corporate end-user documentation.

Vanilla OTC FX options (purchased puts and calls on CAD versus USD, EUR, or CNH) as permitted corporate hedges protecting Amazon FBA settlement conversion prices; speculative barrier or exotic structures are discouraged and require enhanced board documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to genuinely non-deliverable offshore currencies (e.g., INR, restricted emerging-market currencies) booked through the bank's international branches; CAD/USD NDFs are not standard Canadian clearing-rail instruments because the Canadian dollar is freely deliverable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Return (Déclaration annuelle de l'entreprise) — mandatory for every Quebec business corporation under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Register, MIFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the annual anniversary date of the corporation's registration or incorporation (fixed calendar anniversary rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an additional late-filing fee of approximately CAD 19.55 (USD 14); failure to file for three consecutive years authorizes the Registrar to issue a notice and administratively strike off (dissolve) the corporation; directors may also incur individual penalties under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (Corporations Canada) — applicable only if the corporation was incorporated federally under the CBCA and is registered as an extra-provincial enterprise in Quebec; not required for a purely provincial QBCA corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the corporation's incorporation anniversary date each year (anniversary rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Filing online is free; paper filing or late filing may incur a service fee of up to CAD 125 (USD 92). Failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Director to send a notice and dissolve the corporation by administrative strike-off under section 233 of the CBCA.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, a corporation must appoint an independent auditor unless it is not a reporting issuer and all shareholders unanimously consent (in writing or by unanimous resolution) to dispense with the auditor; in practice, this dispensation is available to private corporations with fewer than 15 shareholders. Reporting issuers and publicly accountable enterprises are always subject to a compulsory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian private enterprises apply Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook Part II); publicly accountable or reporting enterprises apply IFRS (Part I). Financial statements filed or used for Canadian and Quebec tax purposes must be prepared in accordance with the elected framework and reconciled to the tax basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At the time of filing the Quebec annual return, the Registraire des entreprises requires confirmation or updating of director and head-office information; any change in these particulars must be declared within 60 days of its occurrence. Under the QBCA Bill 34 regime, the corporation must maintain an internal Register of Individuals with Significant Control (RISC) and update it within 30 days after learning of a change in a significant control interest; this register is kept at the registered office and is subject to statutory inspection by the Registrar and shareholders. Note that Quebec's RISC obligation has been subject to transitional suspension and extension orders — compliance counsel must confirm the precise enforceability window in force on the actual filing date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110–440 (CAD 150–600) per annum for a commercial registered-office and registered-agent mandate in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,100–3,700 (CAD 1,500–5,000) for a review engagement if the audit is dispensed by unanimous shareholder consent; USD 3,700–11,100 (CAD 5,000–15,000) for a full independent statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined general rate 26.5% (federal 15.0% + Quebec 11.5%); an eligible Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation (CCPC) is taxed at a combined 12.2% (federal 9.0% + Quebec 3.2%) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, with the reduced rates phased out when group taxable capital exceeds CAD 10 million (Quebec) / CAD 15 million (federal); a non-resident-owned subsidiary is generally not a CCPC and is taxed at 26.5%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction (effective 9% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income); 13% federal general rate reduction; 10% federal provincial tax abatement; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit at 35% for qualifying CCPCs (20% non-refundable for non-CCPCs); Quebec small business deduction (effective 3.2% rate); Quebec e-commerce and digital-economy tax credits (10% investment tax credit for qualifying online retail platforms); partial income tax exemption for qualifying manufacturing and processing profits; the general rate reduction and small business deduction are unavailable to a personal-services business and to corporations controlled by non-residents
